title: Own runoff history cut annual error by 5.1% after regional history at 185 south-east Australian catchments in 2001-2021
abstract: We tested whether runoff history from other catchments can replace a catchment's own previous-year runoff after detailed weather controls. We used CAMELS-AUS v2.03 at 185 south-east Australian catchments, with 3545 test targets in 2001-2021. Up to ten nearby donors were selected by distance, with mapped watershed overlap excluded. Four ridge models were tuned before 2001 and then fitted using only earlier targets. Own runoff history cut normalized squared error by 8.61% after weather and by 5.10% after weather plus regional history. The latter conditional 95% shared-year block interval was 3.53% to 6.65%. Complete flow records, more distant donors and a fixed penalty retained positive own-history gains. The regional gain beyond own history was sensitive to the penalty. An exact Gaussian example produced a 4.99% own-history gain from a single shared state with no local persistent state. Thus the field result shows added information, but it cannot locate the physical memory or explain the persistent runoff loss after 1997. This is reconstruction with observed target-year weather, not lead forecasting. Short time support, source errors, model form, noisy donors and conditional uncertainty limit inference. Code, source hashes, aggregate errors, uncertainty samples, an independent solver audit and raw-source repeat checks are supplied. External source records stay outside the bundle.

display.caption: Four annual runoff models on common targets at 185 south-east Australian catchments. Own history retains a 5.10 percent error gain after regional history. Intervals are conditional shared-year block intervals.
Own-history gains after regional history remain positive across planned checks. These estimates do not identify a physical memory source.
